rig_create.description: Create a new rig with this `POST /rigs` body, then run on it. Returns 409 `sandbox_name_conflict` if the name is in use.

session.description: FIFO lane on the rig. Runs in one session start in creation order, one at a time. Runs in different sessions run in parallel. Default `default`.

command.description: Shell command. Amika runs it with `bash -e -o pipefail`.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum run time of the command, in milliseconds. The clock starts when the command process starts. At the limit, the conclusion is `timed_out`.

queue_timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait from creation until the command process starts, in milliseconds. The wait includes the session queue, rig start, and workspace setup. At the limit, the conclusion is `queue_timed_out`. Omit for no limit.

rig_status_on_finish.description: Status to give the rig when its last incomplete run finishes. If more than one run sets it, the run that started last decides. Omit to restore the rig's status from before the runs.

cwd.description: Working directory of the command. Absolute, or relative to the agent directory (`AMIKA_AGENT_CWD`). Default: the agent directory.

rig_id.description: Rig the run runs on. Null after the rig is deleted.

rig_name.description: Name of the rig. Null after the rig is deleted.

session.description: Session (FIFO lane) of the run on the rig.

status.description: `queued`: waiting for its session, the rig, or the workspace. `in_progress`: the command started. `completed`: finished; see `conclusion`.

controller_phase.description: Detailed step of the run, for progress displays. Use `status` for logic.

conclusion.description: Result of a `completed` run. Null before completion. `success`: exit code 0. `failure`: non-zero exit code. `cancelled`: cancelled by request. `timed_out`: the command exceeded `timeout_ms`. `queue_timed_out`: the command did not start within `queue_timeout_ms`. `error`: Amika could not run the command.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the command. Null if the command did not exit.

workspace.description: Where the command runs. `rig`: the rig's own files. `git_checkout`: a fresh checkout of `repository_url` at `revision`, made for GitHub Actions runs.

cwd.description: Working directory as requested. Null: the agent directory (`AMIKA_AGENT_CWD`).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum run time of the command, in ms.

queue_timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait before the command starts, in ms. Null: no limit.

rig_status_on_finish.description: Status to give the rig when its last incomplete run finishes. If more than one run sets it, the run that started last decides. Omit to restore the rig's status from before the runs.

started_at.description: When the run left the queue.

CommandRun.description: One shell command on one rig. Amika records its lifecycle, output, and exit code.

sequence.description: Position of the event in the run's output. Starts at 1.

stream.description: `stdout` or `stderr` of the command, or `system` for messages from Amika about the run.

CommandRunEvent.description: One chunk of output from a command run.

CommandRunSource.description: Why the run exists. Set at creation. Filter by it with `source_kind` and `source_id`.

CommandRunSourceGithubActions.description: Created by a GitHub Actions workflow step.

CommandRunSourceGithubActionsRunner.description: Runs a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner that Amika started for a queued job.

step.description: Index of the job step. Null for the finish run, which only applies the job's `rig_status_on_finish`.

CommandRunSourceJob.description: One step of a job run.

schedule.description: 5-field cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), or `@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly`, `@monthly`, `@yearly`. Fires must be at least 5 minutes apart.

timezone.description: IANA time zone to read `schedule` in, with DST. Default `UTC`.

CronTrigger.description: Start a job run at each time that `schedule` matches.

credential.description: The host's secret, whole and opaque. Sent as `x-amika-host-token` when the host dials the gateway.

generation.description: How many times this host's credential has been replaced. The gateway fences a stale connection with it, so a daemon that reconnects sends the generation it enrolled with.

gateway_url.description: The WebSocket address to dial, path included.

transport_mode.description: Always `tunnel`. A `listen` host is refused: it binds a port and is reached at its registered URL.

steps.description: Commands of each job run, in order.

rig_status_on_finish.description: Status to give the rig when the job run ends, after success or failure. When set, the rig stays up between steps. Omit to restore the rig's status from before the job run.

overlap_policy.description: `skip` (default): do not start a scheduled job run while an earlier run of this job is `pending` or `running`; record it as `skipped`. `allow`: start it.

next_run_at.description: Next time the trigger fires. Amika starts the job run within 30 seconds of it. Null while the job is paused.

Job.description: A trigger and an ordered list of steps. Each time the trigger fires, the job starts a job run. Read past job runs with `GET /job-runs?job_id=…`.

scheduled_at.description: Time the schedule fired, or the request time for `manual`. Compare with `created_at` to see the delay.

status.description: `pending`: recorded; no step started. `running`: a step's run, or the finish run, did not complete. `succeeded`: every step concluded `success`. `failed`: a step did not succeed, or Amika could not create its run; later steps did not start. `skipped`: `overlap_policy` dropped it. `cancelled`: `POST /job-runs/{id}/cancel` stopped it; later steps did not start.

current_step.description: Index of the step in progress, or of the step that ended the job run.

steps.description: The job's steps when the job run was recorded. Later changes to the job do not change them.

command_run_ids.description: One command run per started step, in step order. Read each with `GET /command-runs/{id}`.

finish_command_run_id.description: Command run that applied the job's `rig_status_on_finish` when no step run could. Null when not necessary.

error.description: Why the job run failed, was skipped, or was cancelled. A `running` job run with an `error` waits for its finish run.

cancel_requested_at.description: When `POST /job-runs/{id}/cancel` was called. A `running` job run with this set starts no more steps, and becomes `cancelled` once its current step and any finish run complete.

rig_id.description: Rig of step 0's run. Null before step 0 has a run, and after the rig is deleted.

rig_name.description: Name of the rig. Null when `rig_id` is null.

created_at.description: When the job run was recorded.

updated_at.description: When the job run last changed.

completed_at.description: When the job run became `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`, or `cancelled`.

JobRun.description: One execution of a job. It runs the job's steps in order on one rig, one command run per step, and stops at the first step that fails.

cloud_account_ref.description: Run the rig in the connected cloud account with this id or name.

runtime.description: With `host_id`, the host runtime to run the rig on (`smol`, `lume`). Omitted, the rig runs on its preset's default runtime on that host. Requires `host_id`.

resources.description: With `host_id`, the rig's resources, in place of a named `size`: 1 to 16 vCPUs, at least 64 MiB of memory in whole MiB, and a disk of at least 1 GiB. Requires `host_id`, and cannot be combined with `size`.

size.description: Providerless sandbox size (for example `a0.m`). Legacy names such as `m` and `medium` are also accepted. The provider is inferred from `provider` or the server default; when omitted, the size defaults to that provider's medium tier. With `host_id`, names one of the host's own sizes instead; a host rig with neither `size` nor `resources` gets 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB of memory and a 20 GiB disk.

amika_api_key.description: The Amika API key the rig gets as `AMIKA_API_KEY`. `{"mode": "new", "scope": "org"}` (default): a new organization key. `{"mode": "new", "scope": "user"}`: a new key for the calling user; a caller with no user cannot use it. `{"mode": "none"}`: no key, and `AMIKA_API_KEY` is not set. A new key is revoked when the rig is deleted.

rig_create.description: Create a new rig with this `POST /rigs` body, then run on it. Returns 409 `sandbox_name_conflict` if the name is in use.

cloud_account_id.description: Run the rig in this connected cloud account (by id). At most one of cloud_account_id, cloud_account_name, cloud_account_ref. Cannot be combined with host_id.

cloud_account_name.description: Run the rig in the connected cloud account with this name; `amika` means Amika Cloud. `provider` narrows the name.

cloud_account_ref.description: Run the rig in the connected cloud account with this id or name.

runtime.description: With `host_id`, the host runtime to run the rig on (`smol`, `lume`). Omitted, the rig runs on its preset's default runtime on that host. Requires `host_id`.

resources.description: With `host_id`, the rig's resources, in place of a named `size`: 1 to 16 vCPUs, at least 64 MiB of memory in whole MiB, and a disk of at least 1 GiB. Requires `host_id`, and cannot be combined with `size`.

size.description: Providerless sandbox size (for example `a0.m`). Legacy names such as `m` and `medium` are also accepted. The provider is inferred from `provider` or the server default; when omitted, the size defaults to that provider's medium tier. With `host_id`, names one of the host's own sizes instead; a host rig with neither `size` nor `resources` gets 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB of memory and a 20 GiB disk.

amika_api_key.description: The Amika API key the rig gets as `AMIKA_API_KEY`. `{"mode": "new", "scope": "org"}` (default): a new organization key. `{"mode": "new", "scope": "user"}`: a new key for the calling user; a caller with no user cannot use it. `{"mode": "none"}`: no key, and `AMIKA_API_KEY` is not set. A new key is revoked when the rig is deleted.

session.description: FIFO lane on the rig. Runs in one session start in creation order, one at a time. Runs in different sessions run in parallel. Default `default`.

command.description: Shell command. Amika runs it with `bash -e -o pipefail`.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum run time of the command, in milliseconds. The clock starts when the command process starts. At the limit, the conclusion is `timed_out`.

queue_timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait from creation until the command process starts, in milliseconds. The wait includes the session queue, rig start, and workspace setup. At the limit, the conclusion is `queue_timed_out`. Omit for no limit.

cwd.description: Working directory of the command. Absolute, or relative to the agent directory (`AMIKA_AGENT_CWD`). Default: the agent directory.

JobStep.description: One command of a job, as a `CreateCommandRunRequest` body without `rig_status_on_finish`. Step 0 must set exactly one rig selector. Later steps must set none: they run on step 0's rig. A `rig_create` name is a prefix: each job run appends `-` and 12 hex characters.

JobTrigger.description: When the job starts a job run. `cron` is the only kind.

next_sequence.description: Send as `after` in the next request. Equals `after` when there are no new events.

items.description: Job runs, newest first. With `latest_per_job`, the latest of each job, sorted by job id.

next_cursor.description: With `latest_per_job`: send as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page. Otherwise always null.
Send as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page.

cloud_account.description: The org's connected cloud account the rig runs in, or null for Amika Cloud.

url.description: The service's address on the rig's host, ending in `/`. It carries no credential.

header.description: The request header the token goes in, as `Bearer <token>`.
